label: Patient records
lead: Most EMRs make you click through visits one at a time. We don’t. A patient’s entire history — prescriptions, labs, vitals, allergies, family links — is on a single page the doctor scrolls. Search works across them all.

Family link a spouse or child
Issue ABHA-linked records from day one

rows.title: The doctor opens the record. The whole patient is on screen.
rows.lead: Allergies and chronic conditions are pinned at the top. Last 3 visits are inline. Active prescriptions are visible without a click. The patient walks in; the doctor is already up to speed.
bullets: Allergies + chronic conditions live in a permanent panel — not buried in notes.
Last 3 visit notes inline. Older visits collapse but are one keypress away.
Lab trends graphed at the visit level — HbA1c over 2 years, no chart-hunting.

rows.title: Find a patient by anything. Phone, partial name, last visit, doctor.
rows.lead: If your front desk can describe the patient, they can find the patient. Phone digits, half a name, the doctor they saw last time, the condition they came in for — the search index covers all of it.
bullets: Phonetic + Devanagari + Latin index — “Banerjee” or “बनर्जी” find the same patient.
Search across notes — “diabetic patient seen by Dr. Sen last March” returns 3 results.
Recent-patients list reorders by who you saw most recently — 90% of returning lookups are top-of-list.

rows.title: Husband, wife, kids: one shared family card.
rows.lead: Indian healthcare is family-driven. A husband’s appointment often reveals a wife’s prescription that needs renewal. Family linking surfaces this — across patients you’ve already seen, without sharing private records by default.
bullets: Link patients to a family. Each member keeps a private record.
Family-level billing — one invoice covering multiple members’ visits.
Recall calendar at the family level — “dental cleanings for all 4 due this month.”

faqs.a: Yes — every patient can have an ABHA created or linked in under 90 seconds at first visit. Records stay yours; the patient controls cross-provider sharing via the consent manager.
We help import a starter set during onboarding — PDF scans get OCRed and the metadata extracted into the patient timeline. Older records remain searchable but uneditable.

faqs.q: Can the patient see their own records?
faqs.a: Yes — a patient app + ABHA-linked access lets them download prescriptions, lab reports, and visit summaries on demand. You control which fields are visible.
